title: Fermihedral: On the Optimal Compilation for Fermion-to-Qubit Encoding
problem: Selecting the optimal fermion-to-qubit encoding for fermionic quantum systems is challenging due to the large search space and its direct impact on circuit implementation cost, gate count, and depth. Current methods lack systematic approaches to explore this optimization space effectively.
motivation: Efficient fermion-to-qubit encoding is essential for practical quantum simulation of fermionic systems in chemistry and materials science, directly affecting quantum algorithm performance and feasibility.
method: The method transforms the problem of choosing the best fermion-to-qubit encoding into a Boolean Satisfiability problem (finding true/false assignments that satisfy constraints), using Pauli algebra—the mathematical framework that describes quantum operations—to express the encoding constraints and objectives. Since the resulting constraints number exponentially, two approximation strategies help find good solutions without needing to evaluate every possibility.
key_novelty: The core contribution is reformulating fermion-to-qubit encoding selection as a Boolean Satisfiability problem (finding true/false values that make logical constraints true), enabling highly-optimized SAT solvers to solve it efficiently.
contributions: Fermihedral compiler framework for optimal fermion-to-qubit encoding discovery
Novel SAT-based formulation of encoding constraints using Pauli algebra
Two approximation strategies for large-scale problem instances
Demonstrated improvements in gate counts, circuit depth, and simulation accuracy on quantum hardware

metrics.speedup: Substantial reductions in implementation costs, gate counts, and circuit depth
metrics.accuracy: Enhanced simulation accuracy on real quantum devices
